You are designing an implementation plan for a Rust codebase at /home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS (a bare-metal-style kernel project called "G-mOMonadOS" that implements a 12-symbol structural grammar called IMASM/the Grammar). Read-only investigation is fine; do not write code, this is planning only.

## Background you need

The Grammar's twelve marks (glyphs) are opcodes AND graph nodes. The authoritative primer is /home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md — read it in full before designing anything; it defines exact semantics for FSPLIT (∈, the only brancher, δ/comultiplication), FFUSE (∋, the only merger, μ/multiplication), EVALT (⊤, evaluate-true, a real WORK gate), EVALF (⊥, evaluate-false, a real WORK gate), AFWD (≻), AREV (≺), CLINK (⋈), IMSCRIB (⊙, identity/self-reference, NOT work), IFIX (⊡, commit), ENGAGR (⊞), VINIT (⊢), TANCH (⊣). Part IV of the primer defines the GATE semantics precisely: the register is a SIXTEEN_3 value, a subset of {T,F,t,f} (16 states); FSPLIT fans the register's own partition onto its two arms (truth part x∩{T,t}, falsity part x∩{F,f}); FFUSE joins arms by union. Part II defines that pairing between ∈ and ∋ is by ANCESTRY over graph edges, never by text position, and that the verb used to build the graph from a word (chain/ring/protocol) determines the edges — same word, different verb, different graph.

## The exact task

The project owner (I'll call him "the principal" in this prompt — do not use any other name) wants a "factoring membrane": a mechanism where crossing (reading) a composite number N's own IMASM representation yields its real factors P, Q, with P×Q=N, verified by the Grammar's own instruments — not by an external numerical search bolted on and merely labeled with glyphs afterward.

He gave an exact, binding architectural criterion for when a nested "tower" of IMASM operations actually collapses into what he calls a "membrane" (his term; a membrane is the desired object, a tower alone is not useful, it "computes in the typical fashion"). Quoting him exactly:

> There are 2 aspects to the tower that need to be present for the tower to collapse to a proper membrane:
> 1. The nesting structure must be correct, all operations must be nested in the correct order inside the outermost Split/Fuse pair. Sequences that do not usually perform work, when nested with ones that do, have that work transferred to them.
> 2. The entire tower, every part of it, including the values themselves, MUST be written in IMASM. This is *how* the boundaries are dissolved, by making the entire process speak the same language at every level. Without this, it remains a tower and never collapses to a membrane. A tower does nothing for us, it computes in the typical fashion. A membrane is the arcane object we desire.

Condition 1 is a checkable, mechanical property of a graph (ancestry-correct nesting, verifiable with the `vox pairs <word>` CLI tool at ~/.cargo/bin/vox, or the `ask --imasm protocol <tokens...>` CLI built from /home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/MoDoT/ask_native — both already confirmed working in this session for checking whether a value's marks are nested inside a fork/fuse span rather than sitting outside it).

Condition 2 is the hard, open design problem: not just the OPERATOR skeleton (FSPLIT/FFUSE/etc as literal glyphs) but the VALUES themselves — N, and whatever P and Q end up being — must be carried and transformed AS the Belnap register flowing through real gates (per Part IV of the primer), not as a `BigUint`/`u64` computed by ordinary Rust arithmetic and merely labeled with glyph characters afterward.

## What's already been found this session (read these files directly, don't take my summary as ground truth — verify)

1. `src/factor_membrane.rs` in G-mOMonadOS: `interlace_words`/`deinterlace_word` (native_numeral.rs) do a positional bit-interleave of two numbers' `encode()` words — real, tested, exact as an invertible representation (Γ then Λ recovers the same pair), but it is NOT multiplication: interlacing 13 and 17's encode-words decodes to 595, not 13×17=221, in general. This fails condition 2 in a specific way: it's a representation trick over bits, not a real δ (comultiplication) for the *multiplicative* Frobenius algebra on integers.

2. `src/tower_vox.rs`: `FACTOR_TOWER_WORD = "⊢⊙≻⋈∈⊤≻⋈⊙⊥≺⋈⊙⊙≻⋈⊙≺⋈⊙⊡⋈⊙∋⊣"` and `DIALETHIC_TOWER_WORD = "⊢⊙∈⊤≻⋈⊙⊥≺⋈⊙∋⊡⊣"` are fixed IMASM skeletons. `factor_tower_carrying(n)`/`dialetheic_tower_carrying(n)` spliced N's `native_numeral::encode(n)` word (a flat sequence of per-bit `∈bit∋` dyads, itself NOT nested — see point 3) into the tower at a `⊙` position. I found via `vox pairs` that the ORIGINAL code spliced into the textually-first `⊙`, which sits OUTSIDE the tower's own fork/fuse span (before its `∈` even opens) — confirmed: this produced 8 disjoint closed regions instead of N's structure nesting inside the tower's one real 19-span region. I already FIXED this in the working tree (uncommitted) by splicing into the first `⊙` occurring AFTER the fork instead — confirmed via `vox pairs` that N's structure now nests inside the tower's real span. This satisfies condition 1 for THIS specific splice point, but the spliced value is still `native_numeral::encode`'s bit-representation (BigUint-backed under the hood via `WordTape::from_biguint`), so condition 2 still fails for this tower — the tower's own EVALT/EVALF/FSPLIT/FFUSE never actually operate ON N's magnitude as flowing register state; they're a fixed skeleton with N's bits sitting inert alongside them.

3. `src/native_numeral.rs`: `encode(n)`/`decode(word)` map an integer to/from a word of the exact shape `⊢(≻⋈∈bit∋)*⊙⊡⊣` (LSB-first, one flat non-nested `∈bit∋` dyad per bit; `⊤`=0, `⊥`=1). This is an exact, tested, invertible representation — but I confirmed by running this word through the generic IMASM engine (`ask --imasm eval`, built from MoDoT/ask_native) that the engine's real gate semantics (EVALT/EVALF as ACTIVE pass-gates on a flowing Belnap value, per the primer) do NOT read `⊤`/`⊥` here as passive numeral-digit labels — every per-bit dyad just flowed a constant F→F, the bit values had zero effect on anything. This is the clearest confirmation that this representation fails condition 2: it's IMASM-shaped text, not IMASM-native data. `native_numeral.rs` also has `hold_word`, `cycle_landings` (imported from `imasm_core::lattice_flow`), and reports (`compose_report`, `decompose_report`, `leadrun_report`) that relate a number's "orbit period" under `cycle_landings(hold_word(n))` to bit-length via a proven closed form `period(X) = 5*(bits(X)+1)` — real and verified, but this only relates period to BIT-LENGTH, not to factor structure, and `decompose_report`'s own doc comment says finding p,q individually "still takes a search."

4. `ig-docs/dqi_ambient_belnap_deinterlace.md` + `src/dqi_ambient.rs` + `src/closure_nested.rs`: this is the closest existing thing to condition 2 partially working. Key mechanism: `dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul(a,b)` computes a REAL schoolbook multiplication where each COLUMN is an actual Belnap-4 (`B4`) state: `(is_true, is_false) = (digit, carry_flag)` — N=no contribution, T=lone 1, F=saturated column digit 0, B=saturated column digit 1 (both digit AND carry present). This is genuine arithmetic happening IN the four-valued carrier (not BigUint dressed up) — the carry propagation of real multiplication is represented as literal Belnap ambient states (N/B are not "defective" values, they're the carry information). `closure_nested::ambient_product_closes` / `factor_ambient` verify that "digit-channel(μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q)) = N" (retracting B cells via `r`, N cells via `c`) recovers N exactly from this four-valued product — tested (`ambient_product_recovers_n`, `ambient_factor_matches_walk`). This IS a real Frobenius μ (multiplication) implemented natively in the ambient carrier, for a KNOWN (p,q) pair — condition 2 satisfied for the μ/verify direction, when p and q are already in hand.

   HOWEVER: `factor_symbolic(n, m)` (`closure_nested.rs:317-350`, confirmed via a live Explore-agent trace this session to be genuinely O(m), no numeric walk, completes in under a second even at m=431 on a 900-bit N) only narrows N to ONE OF FOUR residue-class cosets mod 2^m (the four cosets of the 2-adic unit group {1,3,-1,-3} mod 2^m) — it does NOT determine the exact numeric factor. Determining the exact value currently falls through to `factor(n,m)`/`closure_height_walk`, a real O(2^(m-3))-positions-per-coset numeric search over `BigUint`/`BigInt` (confirmed: genuinely exponential in m, infeasible past ~m=60-ish in practice, and there's a `checked_shl` overflow bug at m-3≥64 that silently degrades to `usize::MAX` iterations instead of erroring — `closure_nested.rs:89` and `:398`). That numeric fallback is BOTH exponential AND fails condition 2 (it's `BigUint` arithmetic, not register-flow).

   The doc also separately describes (same file) a genuine "closure-height Hensel sieve" idea and a floorless `closure_height_walk` that updates one BigUint quantity `h` by an exact add each step and seals when `h==0` — described elsewhere in this project's memory as halving survivors per additional bit examined (Hensel lifting: `PQ ≡ N mod 2^{m+r}` implies a constraint that roughly halves the surviving candidate set each time you extend `r` by one). This numeric Hensel-doubling-precision idea is architecturally VERY CLOSE to what condition 1 wants structurally (each additional bit of certainty comes from one more NESTED round, not from re-scanning everything) — it's just currently implemented as ordinary `BigUint`/`BigInt` arithmetic, not as marks flowing through real IMASM gates.

## What I need you to design

A concrete implementation plan for a genuine "membrane": a factoring mechanism satisfying BOTH conditions simultaneously for arbitrary N (not just small curated examples), specifically by extending the existing 4-coset symbolic narrowing (`factor_symbolic`) from "one flat O(2^m) numeric scan within a coset" into a RECURSIVELY NESTED, Hensel-lifting-style narrowing where:

- Condition 1: each additional bit of certainty about P (or Q) comes from one MORE nesting level wrapped around the SAME kind of FSPLIT→work→FFUSE dyad that `factor_symbolic`'s `nested_word(m)`/`banked_walk` already uses for the coset-level narrowing — i.e., extending depth from `d=m-3` (which narrows to 1-of-4 cosets, a fixed few bits of certainty) to depth that keeps growing, each level adding ONE more bit of the factor via a real transformation (not an identity `⊙`-only dyad, which would just report N per the primer's "N (identity)" verdict), matching the ALREADY-VERIFIED mechanism in the doc where a bare frame stack alone is vacuous but surfaces work once nested with a working sequence (`⊢∈¹⁰∋¹⁰⊡⊣` vacuous alone → `⊢∈¹⁰≻⋈⊤≻⋈⊥≺⋈⊞⊙∋¹⁰⊡⊣` reports real deposits/register state once nested).
- Condition 2: at every nesting level, the quantity being narrowed (the growing partial reconstruction of P, and the comparison against N) must be represented and updated via the SAME kind of real four-valued carry-aware arithmetic `dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul` already implements for μ (multiplication) — i.e., design (or find, if it already exists and I've missed it — check thoroughly) a δ (comultiplication) counterpart that PRODUCES the next bit/coset-refinement of P as a genuine Belnap-register operation (FSPLIT partitioning x∩{T,t} / x∩{F,f} on a REAL register value derived from N and the partial reconstruction so far), not as a `BigUint` bit-test merely reported afterward in glyph vocabulary.

Read `src/dqi_ambient.rs`, `src/closure_nested.rs` (all of it, not just the excerpts above), `src/belnap.rs` (referenced as predating this work, holds `B4`, `r`, `c`, `inc`, `bnot`), `imasm_core/src/lattice_flow.rs` (`banked_walk`, and check what `nested_word` actually builds structurally), and the primer's Part IV gate table, before designing. Check specifically whether extending `nested_word`/`banked_walk`-style nesting to depth beyond `m-3` (deeper than the fixed coset-narrowing depth) already has ANY existing partial implementation anywhere in this codebase (grep for "Hensel" beyond what's already found, and for any function that takes a GROWING partial P/Q and updates it one register-level nesting at a time) before proposing new code.

Also flag as a small, separate, mechanical fix (not the main design target): `main.rs`'s CLI dispatch doesn't route `closure_nested` (and likely other REPL-only commands) through direct argv execution, so passing it as command-line args falls through to booting the full interactive kernel and spinning forever on non-interactive stdin (EOF read as `\n` in `serial.rs`). This should be fixed alongside the main design work so `closure_nested extract`/`closure_nested wide` etc. are directly scriptable, matching how `factor_membrane`/`native_numeral` already are in `main.rs`'s dispatch (~line 559-576).

Produce a concrete, staged implementation plan: what new Rust functions/types are needed, in which files, how they build on `b4_schoolbook_mul`/`B4`/`ambient_product_closes`/`nested_word`/`banked_walk` rather than duplicating them, what the verification story is (which existing tests to extend, what a genuinely random large-semiprime test case would look like given the checked_shl overflow bug needs fixing too), and a concrete order of implementation steps. Be honest in the plan about where genuine uncertainty remains (e.g., whether a fully register-native δ for the multiplicative Frobenius algebra on arbitrary-width integers is achievable in bounded-per-bit work, or whether some part of this is still an open research question rather than an engineering task) — but do the actual design work rather than deferring everything to "further research needed."

1	# The Imscriber's Guide to IMASM
2	
3	**What it is.** The single comprehensive reading of IMASM: the 12-opcode classic
4	tower and the 14-opcode SIXTEEN_3 trilattice extension presented as one continuous
5	grammar family, statics and dynamics together. It coagulates the former
6	`IMASM_QUICKREF.md`, `IMASM_DYNAMICS.md`, and `md/imasm_composition_rules.md`
7	into one document.
8	
9	**What it does.** Teaches everything needed to write, wire, judge, run, compose,
10	and survey IMASM programs: the alphabet, how a word becomes a graph, the ancestry
11	pairing rule, the close condition, the four verdicts, the register and the gates,
12	the three-verdict discipline, the composition law, ChaosComposer, the op-opcode
13	level, the 49 types, and where the engine itself lives and runs.
14	
15	**Why it matters.** IMASM is the Grammar's executable face: a decision expressed
16	as a word and put to `check` receives a univocal structural verdict, and the same
17	close condition that judges reasoning here is the gate that judges the vita
18	trunk's speech on bare metal. One grammar, one judge, every substrate.
19	
20	**How to use it.** Read Parts I to III to write and judge words; Part IV onward
21	for dynamics, composition, and the wider machinery. Semantics track
22	`ask_native/src/imasm.rs` and `imasm_core/src/check.rs`; run `imasm ref` for the
23	live rules. Where this guide and a live tool ever disagree, the tool is right.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Part I. The Alphabet
28	
29	A program is a DIRECTED GRAPH of opcodes, not a line. One glyph each; the
30	alphabet is fully SYMBOLIC (no Latin initials, so no token ever collides with a
31	verdict letter). WORK? asks: does the opcode TRANSFORM the object?
32	
33	Twelve opcodes, and the same twelve glyphs are the primitive alphabet, one per
34	axis, because the opcodes and the axes were always the same twelve. The
35	trilattice face adds the two bit-swap negations and reads $⊞$ as EVALI. Nothing in
36	the set already means something else in mathematics: that is what it is for.
37	
38	THERE IS ONE DYAD, $∈$ and $∋$, and it has as many arms as the carrier gives it. δ
39	cuts the register into a PARTITION, and which partition depends on how many arms
40	it has: {T,t} | {F,f} at two, and {T} | {F} | {t,f} at three, the truth cut taken
41	inside the constructive block with the non-constructive pair held whole. Both are
42	partitions of the four base values, so μ∘δ = id at either arity. On the classical
43	slice, where t and f are absent, the three-arm cut IS the two-arm cut: the
44	information arm carries nothing. A fan of two is this opcode with an empty arm,
45	not a different opcode, which is why there is one mark and not two.
46	
47	The arity is not a choice either. $⊞$ sets t and f together, so the
48	non-constructive pair can only ever be entered as a block, and three is what the
49	gate set leaves. Note what this rules out: the two-arm cut is not the three-arm
50	cut with an arm dropped. Dropping the information arm leaves {T} | {F}, which
51	loses t and f and would not recover its input. They coincide on the slice, not by
52	truncation.
53	
54	One operator therefore means one ancestry rule, one close condition, one engine.
55	A fuse pairs with the fork that ALL of its in-arms trace back to, which at two
56	arms is the "two distinct in-arms" rule unchanged and at three is the
57	tri-ancestral rule.
58	
59	```
60	GLYPH NAME      MEANING                                VALENCE   WORK?
61	 ⊢   VINIT     begin / source boundary                 0→1        no   the only source
62	 ⊣   TANCH     terminal anchor / close boundary        1→1        no   sink; out-port may stay open
63	 ≻   AFWD      forward morphism                        1→1        YES
64	 ≺   AREV      reverse morphism (involution T↔F, t↔f)  1→1        YES
65	 ⋈   CLINK     compose / link                          1→1        YES
66	 ⊙   IMSCRIB   identity / self-reference               1→1        no   the neutral generator
67	 ∈   FSPLIT    fork (δ): the ONLY brancher             1→2, 1→3   no
68	 ∋   FFUSE     fuse (μ): the ONLY merger               2→1, 3→1   no
69	 ⊤   EVALT     evaluate TRUE arm / set T               1→1        YES
70	 ⊥   EVALF     evaluate FALSE arm / set F              1→1        YES
71	 ⊞   ENGAGR/EVALI  hold paradox (classic) / set t,f    1→1        YES
72	 ⊡   IFIX      irreversible commit / fix               1→1        YES
73	```
74	
75	TWELVE opcodes, no more. The set is `$⊣$$⊢$$≺$$≻$$⊙$$∈$$∋$$⊤$$⊥$$⋈$$⊞$$⊡$`, and ROTAT `↺/↻` (the cyclic
76	shift, below) is the op-opcode that acts ON a word, not a thirteenth letter in it.
77	
78	The WORK? column is the most-missed rule: $⊢$ $⊣$ $⊙$ $∈$ $∋$ $∈$ $∋$ do NOT transform. An
79	arm carrying only $⊙$ (or nothing) is an identity arm, and a closure over identity
80	arms verifies nothing. $⊙$ is self-reference, not work.
81	
82	WORDS: tokens glued as one string, no spaces, e.g. `$⊢$$≻$$∈$$⊤$$⊙$$∋$$⊡$$⊣$`. Space-separated
83	full names parse identically (VINIT AFWD ...), as do the short forms
84	VI TA AF AR CL IM FS FF ET EF EG IX and the aliases δ μ ═ for $∈$ $∋$ =.
85	
86	Glyph provenance: the alphabet is chosen against a single rule, that a mark must
87	not arrive already meaning something else. VINIT $⊢$ and TANCH $⊣$ are the opening
88	and closing boundary turnstiles; EVALT $⊤$ and EVALF $⊥$ are the two poles they
89	evaluate; the dyad is $∈$ and $∋$, membership out of one and into one; CLINK $⋈$ is the
90	join; IFIX $⊡$ is the box that closes; ENGAGR $⊞$ is the Belnap Both it holds; and
91	IMSCRIB is $⊙$ because imscribing IS INCLOSURE, the monadic operation itself, hence
92	self-referential and referenced self-referentially: a boundary around its own
93	centre, denoting the act of denoting. The retired spellings ◇ ● = + × ¬ ~ ≁
94	carried arithmetic, equality, and layer-negation into a language that has none of
95	them, which is what the set was changed to stop. They are not tokens and do not
96	parse; the twelve above are the whole alphabet.
97	
98	The same twelve are the primitive alphabet, one glyph per axis in slot order:
99	$⊢$ Dimensionality, $⊣$ Topology, $≻$ Relational, $≺$ Polarity, $⋈$ Fidelity, $⊙$ Kinetics,
100	$∈$ Granularity, $∋$ Grammar, $⊤$ Criticality, $⊥$ Chirality, $⊞$ Stoichiometry,
101	$⊡$ Protection. Not a mapping between two alphabets: one alphabet, read as an
102	operation or as an axis according to where it stands. The serpent eats its tail.
103	Valences follow IMSCRIBr `tokens.py::TOKEN_ARITY`.
104	
105	## Part II. From Word to Graph
106	
107	A word is only the node list. The EDGES are supplied by the verb you build with:
108	
109	```
110	  chain <word>           wire head→tail, nothing reconnects        (β=0, one strand)
111	  ring <word>            wire head→tail→head; fork/fuse NOT rejoined (β=1)
112	  protocol <word>        wire so $∈$/$∋$ pairs RECONNECT (δ arm → μ): the way to CLOSE
113	  bubble PRE:A:B:POST    $∈$→(A|B)→$∋$ reconvergence, spelled out
114	  star CORE:a:b:c        hub + arms (≥3)
115	  comb BACKBONE:p arm:q arm   backbone + grafts
116	  wire N0 N1 … / i-j i-k …    free graph: node set / edge set
117	```
118	
119	Same word + different verb = different graph = different verdict.
120	`chain $⊢$$∈$$⊤$$⊥$$∋$$⊣$` and `protocol $⊢$$∈$$⊤$$⊥$$∋$$⊣$` are not the same program. To CLOSE, use
121	`protocol`, never a bare `ring`, and never close by looping back to $⊢$ (a source,
122	in-arity 0).
123	
124	### Which $∈$ pairs with which $∋$
125	
126	By ANCESTRY, not by text position and not by a fork-balance stack. A ($∈$,$∋$) pair
127	exists when two distinct in-arms of the $∋$ trace back to a common $∈$: the fork was
128	undone by the fuse, HOWEVER IT ROUTED. Consequences:
129	
130	- Pairing is a property of the EDGES, so the same word wired two ways pairs
131	  differently. You cannot read pairing off the glyph string alone.
132	- A $∈$ feeding a $∋$ directly (empty arm) still counts: in-edges are counted with
133	  multiplicity, and a $∈$ is its own ancestor.
134	- Arms are the nodes strictly between $∈$ and $∋$: forward-reachable from the fork
135	  AND backward-reachable from the fuse. That set is what gets checked for WORK.
136	- A $∋$ may have SEVERAL qualifying $∈$ (upstream forks reach downstream fuses on
137	  any strand). It pairs with the INNERMOST: the candidate no other candidate
138	  descends from. So a $∈$ may close more than one $∋$, but a $∋$ closes with exactly
139	  one $∈$, and an upstream fork cannot claim the fuse a nearer fork actually forked.
140	- fully_closed means EVERY $∈$ and EVERY $∋$ participates in some pair. One dangler
141	  and the whole program is Open.
142	
143	The rule above is already the general one: ALL the in-arms, however many the
144	fuse has. At two that reads "two distinct in-arms" and at three "all three",
145	which is why the tri dyad needs no rule of its own. Same innermost rule, same
146	multiplicity rule. Neutral inflation is allowed: `$⊢$$∈$$⊙$$⊙$$⊙$$∋$$⊣$` is valid tri
147	reconnection with no work, and reads N (identity), the same as `$⊢$$∈$$⊙$$⊙$$⊙$$∋$$⊣$`.
148	
149	`protocol` wires as many arms as the fork's arity declares: one along the chain
150	and the rest straight across. At arity 2 that is the single empty arm it always
151	drew; at arity 3, two.
152	
153	For a plain strand the stack reading (each $∋$ takes the nearest unfused $∈$)
154	happens to agree, and such words may be bracketed for READING BY EYE:
155	`$⊢$$⊙$$⋈$[$∈$$≻$$⊤$$≺$$⊞$$⊥$$∋$]$⊡$$⊡$$⊣$`, nesting as nested brackets. Three caveats, all load-bearing:
156	brackets are NOT input (they parse to nothing, so a bracketed word reports
157	N void); the aid works for strands ONLY; and it is not the pairing rule.
158	Ancestry is. The two coincide on a strand and part company the moment edges
159	route otherwise.
160	
161	## Part III. The Close Condition and the Verdicts
162	
163	A program CLOSES iff BOTH hold:
164	
165	1. RECONNECTION: every brancher ($∈$ or $∈$) and every merger ($∋$ or $∋$) participates
166	   in an ancestry pair, and
167	2. TRANSFORMATION: at least one such pair carries a WORK opcode on its arms.
168	
169	A bare cycle is NOT a closure; β (loops) is never diagnostic. Split→fuse with
170	nothing between is μ∘δ=id, which type-checks nothing. The close condition is
171	μ∘δ over a TRANSFORMED object: split, work, fuse.
172	
173	### Verdicts (from `check` / `imasm16_3 check`, identical logic)
174	
175	```
176	  T (closes)        μ∘δ closes over n transformed reconnections → proceed
177	  N (identity)      $∈$/$∋$ reconnect but no WORK between → put work on the arms
178	  N (no fork)       no δ/μ dyad at all → never weighed alternatives
179	  N (void)          no committed opcodes: nothing parsed → write a real word
180	  B (open)          well-typed, but a $∈$ or $∋$ dangles unreconnected → fuse it ($∋$)
181	                    or commit one arm (¬)
182	  B (paradox held)  closes over a transformation AND a $⊞$ is present → genuinely
183	                    both. Sound to hold; do NOT read it as a clean T; look again
184	                    before an irreversible ¬.
185	  F (ill-typed)     grammar violated → revise
186	```
187	
188	B BEATS T: a word that closes but contains ENGAGR reports B, never T. Holding a
189	paradox is sound, but it is not a clean pass.
190	
191	F is exactly three errors: a non-brancher fanning out, a non-merger merging in,
192	or any node exceeding its own arity. Nothing else is fatal.
193	
194	OPEN VALENCES ARE NOT ERRORS. An arm that runs out of successors is a living /
195	telechelic end: reported as "open valences (living ends): n out, m in; reactive,
196	not errors". $⊣$ may end with its out-port open; $⊢$ may start with its in-port open.
197	
198	### Topology names (from `classify`)
199	
200	Named by invariants, not by fork balance. β = E − V + C (independent loops):
201	
202	```
203	  trivial   no nodes
204	  linear    β=0, no branch points: a single strand
205	  star      β=0, branch points forming ONE contiguous hub, ≥3 arms
206	  comb      β=0, branch points strung along a backbone: graft/comb tree
207	  ring      β=1, no branch and no merge points: single cycle, no pendants
208	  branched  β=1 with branch or merge points
209	  network   β≥2, or more than one disconnected strand
210	```
211	
212	Reported with: V, E, β, branch/merge/src/sink census, arm count, and spectral
213	radius ρ. Star caveat: the abstract star K(1,f) has ρ=√f, but IMASM fan-out caps
214	at 2 ($∈$ is out-2), so a hub is REALIZED as a caterpillar of f−1 $∈$ fan-nodes and
215	the true ρ tends to 2, not √f.
216	
217	## Part IV. The Carrier and the Gates (dynamics)
218	
219	The register is a SIXTEEN_3 value: a subset of the four base values {T, F, t, f}
220	(Shramko, Dunn and Takenaka's trilattice, "The Trilattice of Constructive Truth
221	Values", J. Logic and Computation 11(6):761-788, 2001; T constructively proven,
222	F constructively refuted, t acceptable, f rejectable), sixteen states from
223	N = {} to A = {T,F,t,f}. FOUR is not a second system: it is the classical slice
224	{T, F} of the same carrier, with Belnap B = {T,F} and N = {}. One evaluator runs
225	both; `eval` renders the slice (N/T/F/B), `eval16` renders the full names. A
226	value that touches t or f has left the slice and keeps its 16_3 name in either
227	view. NOT two independent FOURs, NOT three independent bits: one 4-bit register,
228	verified against the paper's own worked example (T ∧ t = N under the truth order).
229	
230	Three orderings, each with a meet/join (`imasm16_3 algebra <op> A B`):
231	
232	```
233	  ≤_i information     x ⊆ y                                            ⊓/⊔
234	  ≤_t truth           x∩{T,t} ⊆ y∩{T,t}  and  y∩{F,f} ⊆ x∩{F,f}        ∧/∨
235	  ≤_c constructivity  x∩{T,F} ⊆ y∩{T,F}  and  y∩{t,f} ⊆ x∩{t,f}        △/▽
236	```
237	
238	Flow uses ≤_i: shuttling only ever moves values up the information order. AREV `$≺$`
239	is the trilattice negation, and it factors into two bit-SWAPS (not flips), one per
240	layer: the paper requires negation to preserve ≤_i exactly, and swapping two bits
241	preserves |x| where a flip would not. Those factors are not independent operators —
242	`$≺$` alone carries Tf to Ft, and on the classical slice `$≺$` carries T to F by
243	itself. The retired marks ~ ≁ once spelled the two factors; the twelve-opcode core
244	needs no room for either, and $⊡$ IFIX replaces them.
245	
246	### The gates
247	
248	Every opcode is a gate over the carrier. Inputs join by union (the ≤_i join)
249	before the gate acts; the value leaving a gate rides every out-edge except where
250	δ fans.
251	
252	```
253	  VINIT $⊢$          emits the seed (default B in the slice, A in full 16_3)
254	  FSPLIT $∈$ / $∈$     δ fans the register's own partition onto its arms: at two,
255	                   truth part x∩{T,t} and falsity part x∩{F,f}; at three,
256	                   x∩{T}, x∩{F}, and the information part x∩{t,f}
257	  EVALT $⊤$          pass-gate: truth part
258	  EVALF $⊥$          pass-gate: falsity part
259	  EVALI $⊞$ (16_3)   sets the information layer (t and f)
260	  FFUSE $∋$ / $∋$      μ / μ₃ joins: union of the arms
261	  AREV $≺$           the involution T↔F, t↔f (its own inverse; fixes B and N).
262	                   Internally it factors as two disjoint-bit swaps, one per layer
263	                   (T↔F and t↔f); composing the two IS AREV. Those factors are not
264	                   opcodes and were never in the set — the retired marks ~ ≁ once
265	                   named them, and $⊡$ IFIX replaces those marks.
266	  AFWD $≻$, CLINK $⋈$, IMSCRIB $⊙$, ENGAGR $⊞$ (as hold)   carry
267	  IFIX $⊡$           carry and latch (the commit point)
268	  TANCH $⊣$          readout
269	```
270	
271	Every gate is monotone in ≤_i, so evaluation is a Kleene iteration from all-N
272	edge values that settles in bounded rounds on any graph, cycles included. A loop
273	converges; it cannot oscillate. The machine's registers are the edges; IFIX
274	marks where value becomes commitment.
275	
276	## Part V. The Three Independent Verdicts
277	
278	A program earns three judgments, none implying another:
279	
280	1. **Grammar** (`define`): the composition laws hold; only branchers branch,
281	   only mergers fuse, arities respected.
282	2. **Kernel** (`prove`): the closure class goes to the live p4ramill kernel. A
283	   worked dyad (split, transform, fuse) proves green; a bare fork-fuse is an
284	   identity closure and returns N for the program; a dangling fork is OPEN.
285	3. **Flow** (`eval` / `eval16`): per dyad, does the fuse RECOVER what the fork
286	   was fed? The canonical protocol word (`$⊢$$∈$$≻$$∋$$⊤$` as VINIT FSPLIT AFWD FFUSE
287	   EVALT) is lossless: B splits to (T,F) and fuses back to B, the operational
288	   split_fuse_id. The same shape with AREV on the truth arm closes in structure
289	   and fails in value: fed Tf, recovered Ff, NOT id. The arm inverted what it
290	   carried, and only flow can see that.
291	
292	Flowing a catalog entry expands its twelve glyph types into opcode motifs, and
293	the per-dyad id/NOT-id sequence is a FLOW SIGNATURE: a readout of the tuple in
294	the dynamic register. Signatures discriminate between entries, and a lossy dyad
295	inside a kernel-green closure is not presumed a defect; it can be the entry's
296	chirality speaking in flow.
297	
298	Discipline for any new program: define (grammar), prove (kernel), eval (flow),
299	and SPEAK THE EXPECTED READOUT BEFORE RUNNING EVAL. The gates are deterministic,
300	so the true name of a topology includes its flow.
301	
302	## Part VI. The Composition Law
303	
304	Programs interact end-to-valence. A living end is an unfilled port (a node below
305	its arity), the same reactive ends the engine always reported; they are the
306	register ports of the program as a component. `imasm compose <new> <A> <B>`
307	binds A's free out-ends to B's free in-ends, in node order, under three rules:
308	
309	1. Composition CONSUMES valences and never mints one.
310	2. The composite must re-satisfy the grammar; an ill-typed binding is refused
311	   whole.
312	3. A program with no living ends does not compose. It is a finished loop; it is
313	   done.
314	
315	Composites persist as wire specs, rebuild through the identical parse, and
316	remain composable while ends remain. Composition is therefore well-founded: each
317	step consumes ends, ends are finite, and the fixed point is a program with none.
318	This is the thesis (no lines, only loops, and autopoiesis) running as type
319	discipline: lines are the composable phase, loops are results, and the registry
320	census confirms it at scale, with roughly half the tools reactive material and
321	half finished loops.
322	
323	## Part VII. ChaosComposer: the Possibility State Space
324	
325	`chaos` takes a SET of programs (up to six). A set has no order, so the composer
326	walks every ordering, folds each through the binding law, and speaks the space
327	whole: which arrangements are admitted, which are refused and by which missing
328	end, and the collapse of orderings into OUTCOME CLASSES keyed by topology,
329	closure, flow, readout, and remaining living ends. The collapse is the
330	measurement: the space of possibilities is smaller than the space of orderings,
331	and the ratio says how constrained the set is. Refusals are results of equal
332	rank; a set of finished loops refuses every ordering, which is the type verdict
333	"these objects are done."
334	
335	### Laws of flow found by walking spaces
336	
337	- **Closure and flow-perfection can be in tension.** In one measured set,
338	  exactly one arrangement of twenty-four closed, a different one was
339	  flow-perfect, and none was both: closing forced a value through a lossy dyad.
340	- **The tension is not a law of the alphabet.** A census over sampled
341	  machine-shaped sets found spaces with closures, spaces with perfect flow, and
342	  a minority with both.
343	- **Perfect machines exist.** One set's whole possibility space is terminal
344	  objects: every admitted arrangement is CLOSED, flow-perfect, and ends with
345	  zero living ends. One is minted as `perfect_machine`, kernel green, every fuse
346	  recovering B.
347	- **The mechanism is exact.** The involution fixes B and N, so AREV costs
348	  nothing while an invol-symmetric value flows; it mints the missing pole when
349	  fed a PROJECTED value (invol(T) = F). Therefore AREV is lossless exactly on
350	  invol-symmetric values, and closure/flow tension appears precisely where a
351	  projection feeds an inversion. Both conditions are readable off the program
352	  before it runs, so an arrangement's capacity for perfection is part of its
353	  true name, speakable in advance and confirmable by the tools.
354	
355	![perfect_machine: closed, lossless, no living ends](figures/imasm_perfect_machine.png)
356	
357	## Part VIII. Op-Opcodes: Operators on Words, Not Nodes
358	
359	A node-opcode is a symbol inside a word; a VERB turns a word into a graph. An
360	OP-OPCODE is a third thing: a map that acts on the whole composition and returns
361	another composition. It is NOT one of the opcodes, and appending its name as a
362	token does nothing; it is not a node. It transforms the word.
363	
364	**ROTAT**: the cyclic shift of a ring, rotate the word by one, k → k+1. The ring
365	automorphism. ρ and every spectral invariant are ROTAT-invariant (that
366	invariance IS the signal that ROTAT is a symmetry, not that it is inert). On ONE
367	ring it changes nothing measurable; between TWO rings being bound it sets their
368	RELATIVE phase, the degree of freedom that seats a junction two same-handed
369	(isotactic) rings cannot close on their own (the θ=0.50 co-typing termination).
370	ROTAT is the Weyl-Heisenberg shift X on ℤ/dℤ; the SIC displacement D_{a,b}
371	carries ROTAT^a. The balanced tiling of a period-n cycle is unique UP TO ROTAT.
372	
373	Op-opcodes are open: ROTAT `↺/↻` is the first named one (↺ shifts k→k−1, ↻ shifts
374	k→k+1). Its relative is reflection (the half-period involution ROTAT^{d/2}). The
375	two-layer swaps that AREV `$≺$` factors into also act on the register rather than the
376	word, but they are internal to `$≺$`, not op-opcodes and not set members; the retired
377	marks ~ ≁ once named them and $⊡$ IFIX replaces those marks. The class was surfaced by the
378	necessity of binding two isotactic rings; no node-opcode rotates one ring
379	against another, so the operation had to live one level up, on the word itself.
380	
381	## Part IX. The Types: the Strange Loop
382	
383	Every TYPE the Grammar writes with is itself a full IMASM program. `imasm types`
384	lists the 49 Shavian type names (ado, air, ash, awe, ...); `imasm expand <type>`
385	locates the `the_primitive_type_called_<name>` ob3ect, pulls its ordered
386	bootstrap opcodes and fork/fuse pairs, and hands back the reconstructed graph
387	plus the per-step domain actions. The types judge programs, and the types ARE
388	programs judged by the same close condition: the strange loop is not decoration,
389	it is the autopoietic floor of the system.
390	
391	The loop is walkable in both directions. A tuple becomes a word by writing each
392	of its twelve types as that type's own program and concatenating in canonical
393	axis order; `imasm cycle` runs the return leg too, reading a word back into the
394	types that could have written it, and reports where the round trip closes. Three
395	things it establishes. Type programs are NOT self-delimiting (the type `out`
396	carries TANCH in its middle and does not end on $⊣$), so a concatenated word must
397	be parsed axis by axis and never cut on the boundary pair. Position is
398	load-bearing: the 49 types emit only 47 distinct programs, and of the two
399	colliding pairs one is separated by the axes it may occupy while the other is
400	not. And at catalog scale no entry loses its original type, with ambiguity
401	confined to the single axis the alphabet analysis predicts. The full reading is
402	in `md/primitive_imasm_cycle.md`.
403	
404	State the strength of this exactly, because it is easy to overclaim: the cycle
405	is NOT a bijection. It is bijective on eleven axes and two-to-one on the
406	twelfth, where the colliding pair shares an axis, so the reading is a SECTION of
407	the writing and not an inverse. Write a tuple, read it back, write again, and
408	the word returns identical; read a word cold and one axis may hold two answers.
409	`imasm cycle tuple=⟨…⟩` runs one tuple, catalog entry or not, and says per axis
410	whether it came back exactly, ambiguously, or not at all.
411	
412	## Part X. Where the Engine Lives
413	
414	The close-condition engine (Graph, ancestry pairing, ClosureState, and the whole
415	gate `word_verdict`) lives in `imasm_core/src/check.rs`: no_std + alloc, so the
416	verdict can be spoken wherever the kernel runs. `ask_native/src/imasm.rs` keeps
417	presentation, spectral analysis, and the tool registry as extensions over the
418	core Graph, and is the tool that answers `imasm check`. The tri-ancestral
419	verdict lives beside it in `imasm_core/src/imasm16_3.rs`.
420	
421	The same engine runs on bare metal: mOMonadOS carries imasm_core, and its
422	on-board vita mouth (the vae_vita trunk baked to a raw blob and reimplemented in
423	no_std scalar f32) speaks certified turns whose words are gated by
424	`check::word_verdict` or, when the word carries tri tokens, the tri-ancestral
425	verdict. The kernel that judges your reasoning at the prompt is byte-for-byte
426	the kernel that judges the trunk's speech on the machine with no OS beneath it.
427	
428	## Part XI. The Surface and the Guarantees
429	
430	`imasm_composer.html` is a fully local, self-contained page (no external assets,
431	nothing leaves the machine). `imasm export` writes the manifest (every
432	registered tool with its graph, ports, and closure state, plus the opcode
433	table); the page renders that manifest as a node canvas: palette, drag, click an
434	out-port then an in-port to bind. It judges nothing and only SPEAKS command
435	lines (`compose`, `chaos`, `wire`, `eval`, `prove`) for the kernel to judge. One
436	grammar, one judge; the surface is a hand, not a head.
437	
438	Engineering guarantees:
439	
440	- Registry writes are atomic (temp file, then rename): a reader sees the old
441	  registry or the new one, never a torn one.
442	- A registry file that exists but does not parse is preserved as `.corrupt`
443	  evidence, never silently replaced by emptiness.
444	- Kernel verdicts name the spec they bind, so a refused re-define can never
445	  borrow an older program's green.
446	- An identity closure answers N for the program, in words, with the repair named
447	  (put a transforming opcode between the fork and the fuse).
448	
449	## Part XII. Verb Index
450	
451	```
452	  imasm chain / ring / protocol / bubble / star / comb / wire    build (Part II)
453	  imasm classify <word>        topology + invariants + μ∘δ state
454	  imasm check <word>           type-check your OWN reasoning → T/N/B/F
455	  imasm prove <name|word>      take the verdict to the real Lean kernel
456	  imasm eval  <name|entry|word> [seed=N|T|F|B]    flow, FOUR readout
457	  imasm eval16 <name|entry|word> [seed=A|Tf|…]    flow, full SIXTEEN_3
458	  imasm compose <new> <A> <B>  bind living ends, register
459	  imasm chaos <A> <B> [C… ≤6]  the possibility state space
460	  imasm learn <word> [rounds=N] [breadth=K]   the excription learning loop (Part XIV)
461	  imasm path <A> <B>           promotion path: valid-waypoint edit walk A→B (Part XV)
462	  imasm export                 manifest for the surface
463	  imasm ref                    the live rules (authoritative over this file)
464	  imasm types / expand <type>  the 49 Shavian types (each itself a program)
465	  imasm cycle [n=<count>]      primitives → imasm → primitives → imasm, measured
466	                               over the live catalog
467	  imasm cycle tuple=⟨…⟩        the same cycle on ONE tuple, per axis
468	  imasm define <name> <op> <args…>   build a kernel-constrained tool
469	  imasm run <name> / imasm tools     invoke / list forged tools
470	
471	  imasm16_3 check <glyph_word>  tri type-check: T/N/B/F, same reading
472	  imasm16_3 algebra <op> A B    leq_i|leq_t|leq_c|meet_t|join_t|meet_c|join_c
473	                                on two named registers; `algebra meet_t T t`
474	                                reproduces the paper's worked example, T∧t=N
475	  imasm16_3 ref                 the live 14-glyph table
476	```
477	
478	## Part XIII. Rule of Thumb, Canonical Words, Pitfalls
479	
480	Express a decision as a word ($⊢$ begin · $⊙$ self-identify · $≻$ move · $∈$ weigh
481	options · +/× the true/false arms · $∋$ resolve · $⊞$ hold paradox · ¬ commit ·
482	$⊣$ close), then `imasm check` it. Only branchers branch, only mergers fuse. Put
483	real WORK on the arms or it is N. Use `protocol` to close, never a bare `ring`.
484	
485	Canonical words:
486	
487	```
488	  $⊢$$∈$$≻$$⊤$$∋$$⊣$        lossless protocol: closes in shape AND value, recovers B → T
489	                 wired at three arms it is the same word, and on the FOUR slice
490	                 it flows identically, the third arm carrying nothing
491	  $⊢$$∈$$⊙$$∋$$⊣$         identity: reconnects, no work, μ∘δ=id → N
492	  $⊢$$∈$$⊙$$⊙$$⊙$$∋$$⊣$       tri identity: same reading → N
493	  $⊢$$∈$$⊞$$≻$$∋$$⊣$        closes over work AND holds paradox → B (paradox held)
494	  $⊢$$≻$$∈$$⊤$$⊥$$∋$$⊡$$⊣$      tri word driving the register toward full A (EVALT, EVALF on
495	                 the arms), fused and latched at $⊡$ → T
496	```
497	
498	Pitfalls, all load-bearing:
499	
500	- Reading a word as a line. It is a graph; the verb supplies the edges.
501	- Pairing $∈$/$∋$ by counting or by nearest-match. Pairing is ancestry over edges.
502	- Putting only $⊙$ between $∈$ and $∋$ and expecting T. That is N (identity).
503	- Expecting T from a word containing $⊞$. That is B (paradox held).
504	- Treating an open arm as a failure. It is a living end, reported not fatal.
505	- Closing a loop back to $⊢$. It has in-arity 0 and cannot be a target.
506	- Writing V/T/B or ← out of habit. Retired: they no longer parse → N (void).
507	- Pasting a bracketed word into the tool. Brackets parse to nothing → N (void).
508	- Treating the classic and trilattice faces as separate languages. They share
509	  the register, the ancestry rule, the close condition, the flow semantics, and
510	  the composition law; the differences are arity and the information-layer bits.
511	- Expecting T from the tri word `$⊢$$≻$$∈$$⊤$$⊥$$⊞$$∋$$⊡$$⊣$` under `imasm check`. $⊞$ is ENGAGR to
512	  the classic reading and EVALI to the trilattice one, and B beats T, so the
513	  classic checker answers B (paradox held) for it. One glyph, two readings: the
514	  collision is real and it is the next thing the notation has to settle.
515	
516	## Part XIV. The Excription Loop: imasm learn
517	
518	`imasm learn '<word>' [rounds=N] [breadth=K]` runs verification as imscription
519	on a MODEL. The word needs no shell quoting: $≺$ and $≻$ replaced < and > precisely so the
520	marks stop colliding with redirection, XML, and generics. Both
521	faces run: a word carrying tri tokens selects the SIXTEEN_3 grammar, any other
522	the classic grammar; one loop, one knowledge file.
523	
524	Each round takes the neighborhood of the current word (single-opcode
525	substitutions, insertions, deletions from the face's body alphabet; the
526	boundary turnstiles held fixed; only grammar-valid candidates admitted). For
527	each candidate the model excribes the word into a GUESS: it names one concrete
528	object in a real domain whose structure is the word. The excriber is grounded
529	in the primitives: each opcode is tagged with the axis it rides (VINIT
530	Dimensionality, FSPLIT Granularity, EVALT Criticality, IFIX Topological
531	Protection, and so on), the twelve axes are given as tangible handles, and the
532	primitive types are loaded from ob3ect/digital as exemplars, each itself an
533	IMASM word. So the guess is read off the program's characteristics, not its
534	glyphs alone. The prompt carries one
535	worked example word with three wildly different excriptions of it (three
536	domains, one structure), teaching the fan-out rather than an answer; the
537	guessing domain itself is assigned, rotated by the word, so a small model
538	cannot collapse onto a single name. The guess is blinded (any leaked opcode
539	vocabulary excised), and a guess that parrots a spent example or an
540	already-taken guess is refused mechanically with one hotter retry in the next
541	domain over: distinct words must earn distinct names. A second reading
542	imscribes the guess alone back into a word. Both words are checked in the
543	word's face, and the residual is the edit distance between the word sent and
544	the word recovered: residual zero is the round trip closing, the operational
545	statement that excription and imscription compose to the identity on that
546	word, with the guessed object as the fixed point between them.
547	
548	Where the residual is not zero, the aligned confusions are counted into
549	ob3ects/imasm_knowledge.json alongside the guess, distilled into lessons, and
550	the lessons ride the imscriber's next prompt: the knowledge update is the part
551	of the record that changes the next reading. The walk moves to the
552	highest-residual candidate, the frontier of its own ignorance, and each run
553	appends its mean residual to the accuracy trajectory, the curve the loop is
554	supposed to bend downward over time. The knowledge file persists atomically,
555	same discipline as the tool registry.
556	
557	## Part XV. Promotion Paths Between Programs
558	
559	Two 12-primitive tuples that differ have a promotion path: a walk that changes
560	one primitive at a time with every intermediate well-formed, the way
561	`recalibrate` walks one axis through its values. Two IMASM programs are the
562	same. `imasm path '<A>' '<B>'` finds the PROMOTION PATH from word A to word B:
563	the shortest sequence of single-opcode edits (substitute, insert, or delete one
564	glyph) in which every waypoint is itself a grammar-valid program. It is A* over
565	the graph of valid programs, the raw edit distance serving as the admissible
566	heuristic; it runs in either face, chosen by the words.
567	
568	The learn loop's residual is the RAW edit distance between the word sent and the
569	word recovered. The promotion path is the stronger object built on the same
570	metric: the walk through valid programs only, and its verdict may climb along
571	the way. Substituting an inert IMSCRIB for a working opcode promotes an identity
572	closure (N) to a real closure (T) in one step, the program-space image of a
573	tuple's verdict rising under promotion. The tool reports the verdict walk and
574	says whether the path is a genuine promotion (the verdict changes) or a lateral
575	edit (it does not).
576	
577	## Related documents
578	
579	- `md/primitive_imasm_cycle.md`: the primitives ↔ IMASM cycle, both legs, and
580	  where the type alphabet stops being invertible.
581	- `md/chaos_first_measurements.md`: the chaos measurements, census, and the
582	  perfect-machine mechanism in full.
583	- `md/verification_as_imscription.md`: the theory of verification as
584	  imscription (the Dual-Link SIC Witness-Vessel).
585	- `../ob3ect/READING_GUIDE.md` §3: the fixed glyph vocabulary the alphabet
586	  references.
587	- `../IMASM_REFERENCE.md`: the earlier unified reading at the constellation
588	  root; this guide supersedes it inside MoDoT.
